history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE — this row duplicates seq 1026 (Tripura Sundari Temple, Matabari/Udaipur); see data/json/1026.json (on the Mac output folder) as the canonical record. No Tripura Sundari Temple exists at Ambassa: Ambassa is the Dhalai-district headquarters town, ~65 km north of the real temple, and no shrine of this name is documented there. The one famous Tripura Sundari Temple (Devi Tripureshwari, the third Mahavidya) stands at Matabari, Udaipur, Gomati district, ~55 km from Agartala; the CSV town 'Ambassa' is wrong and has been corrected. It is one of the 51 Shakta pithas (Sati's right foot fell here), built in 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya after a dream-vision, in Bengali Ek-ratna style on a tortoise-hump hillock (Kurma Pitha). The sanctum holds a 5-ft Tripura Sundari idol and the 2-ft 'Chhoto-Ma' (Chandi), once carried to battlefields. The state of Tripura is named after this temple. A Diwali mela draws 200,000+ pilgrims; a Rs 34.43 crore PRASHAD-scheme redevelopment was inaugurated on 22 September 2025.
